title: Memorandum On The Movements Of P.P. Otlichin, Soviet Diplomatic Courier

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch. Station.
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE G.&.N°.B..REGISTRY. No D. 5833 Date 24 / 1 / 34）
Date April 23, 1934
Subject (in full) Peter Otlichin, Soviet employee.
Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by S.B.Lu S./
Peter Otlichin, 30, U.S.S.R. diplomatic courier, arrived
at Shanghai from Moscow via Kobe, Japan, on April 20, 1934, by
the s.s. "Nagasaki Maru", accompanied by another courier B.Vikhman.
P. Otlichin holds a diplomatic passport No. 2758 issued by the
Commissariat for Foreign Affairs on February 14, 1934. This
passport bears a Chinese visa issued by the Chinese Embassy in
Moscow. P. Otlichin stated in the alien declaration form
that he is proceeding to the U.S.S.R. Embassy at Nanking.
Otlichin was met at the wharf by M.A. Targansky, secretary
to the U.S.S.R. Consulate-General at Shanghai.
DTcheremshansky
D. S.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 5833
Date 14 / 12 / 34

S. 2, Special Branch
December 14, 1934.

Memorandum on the movements of P.P. Otlichin, Soviet
diplomatic Courier.

Peter Petrovitch Otlichin, 30, U.S.S.R. diplomatic
courier arrived in Shanghai from Moscow via Vladivostok
and Kobe, Japan, on December 11, 1934 by ss. President
Jefferson, accompanied by another courier named Karl
*Pedrikson. P. Otlichin holds a diplomatic passport No. 2758
issued by the Commissariat for Foreign Affairs on February 14,
1934. This passport bears a Chinese visa issued on
10-11-34 by the Chinese Embassy in Moscow. P. Otlichin
stated on the Alien declaration form that he is proceeding
to the U.S.S.R. Embassy at Nanking, where he will stay for
about one week.
